questions.stem: Choose the correct article: '______ Eiffel Tower is one of the most famous landmarks in the world.'

options.option_text: A (wrong: 'A Eiffel Tower' — specific named landmark must use THE)
An (wrong: 'An' is used before vowel sounds, but Eiffel Tower needs THE as a definite reference)
The (correct: 'The' is used before the names of famous buildings, monuments, towers, and bridges ✓)
No article (wrong: specific named landmarks always take 'The')

questions.explanation: C is correct. THE is used before names of: (1) famous buildings and monuments (the Eiffel Tower, the Taj Mahal, the White House); (2) rivers (the Ganga); (3) mountain ranges (the Himalayas); (4) oceans/seas (the Pacific); (5) deserts (the Sahara); (6) newspapers (the Times of India). NOT used before individual mountains (Mount Everest, not the Mount Everest).

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 'She is ______ honest officer who always upholds justice.'

options.option_text: a (wrong: 'a honest' — the 'h' in 'honest' is silent; it makes a vowel sound /ɒ/, so 'an' is used)
an (correct: 'an honest officer' — 'honest' begins with a silent H, so sounds like /ɒnɪst/; 'an' used before vowel sounds ✓)
the (wrong: 'the honest officer' — would imply a specific previously mentioned officer; not correct here)
no article (wrong: an article is required before a singular countable noun like 'officer')

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'AN' is used before words that BEGIN WITH A VOWEL SOUND (not letter). 'Honest' = /ɒnɪst/ — the H is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound → 'AN honest'. Other silent-H words: an hour, an heir, an honour, an herb (British pronunciation). Contrast: 'a hotel' — H is pronounced /h/, so 'a' is used.

questions.stem:
Choose the sentence with CORRECT article use:
A. She plays a piano every evening.
B. She plays the piano every evening.
C. She plays piano every evening.
D. She plays an piano every evening.

options.option_text: A (wrong: 'a piano' would mean one of many pianos; playing a musical instrument uses 'the')
B (correct: 'play THE instrument' is the idiom — not 'play a piano/a guitar'; THE is used for musical instruments ✓)
C (wrong: no article before a singular countable noun in this context is incorrect)
D (wrong: 'an piano' — piano begins with a consonant sound /p/, so 'a' not 'an')

questions.explanation: B is correct. THE is used with musical instruments when referring to playing them: play THE piano, play THE guitar, play THE violin. This is a fixed idiom. Contrast sports: play cricket (no article), play football (no article). 'She plays A piano' would mean she physically plays one of several pianos, which is odd.

questions.stem: Which sentence has INCORRECT article use?

options.option_text: He was elected the President of India. (correct: 'the President' — specific title/office ✓)
Man is mortal. (correct: no article needed for abstract/generic human — 'Man' used generically ✓)
The gold is a precious metal. (incorrect: 'gold' as a material/substance doesn't take THE when used generically — should be 'Gold is a precious metal' without THE ✓)
I have a dog and a cat. (correct: 'a/an' for introducing non-specific countable nouns ✓)

questions.explanation: C is the incorrect sentence. 'The gold is a precious metal' is wrong. When using a noun generically (referring to the entire category), don't use 'the': 'Gold is a precious metal ✓.' 'THE gold' would refer to specific gold (the gold in this vault). Compare: 'The gold found in that mine is of high quality' — here 'the gold' is specific gold, so THE is correct.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 'He returned home after ______ year of working abroad.'

options.option_text: a (wrong: 'year' begins with the /j/ sound (consonant sound), so 'a year' is correct — but 'a year' means one year, while the sentence needs 'a' ✓; wait — 'a' IS correct here; but we need to pick the right one: 'year' starts with consonant /j/ sound → 'a year')
an (wrong: 'an year' — 'year' begins with consonant sound /j/ (like 'yell'), so 'a' not 'an' is correct)
the (wrong: 'the year' would imply a specific year already mentioned)
no article (wrong: an article is needed before the singular countable noun 'year')

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'A year' — 'year' begins with the consonant sound /j/ (like 'yes', 'yell'). Even though it starts with the vowel letter 'y', the SOUND is consonant → use 'a'. Similarly: 'a university' (not 'an university') — begins with /j/ sound; 'a European country' — begins with /j/ sound. The rule is based on SOUND, not spelling.

questions.stem:
Identify the sentence with CORRECT article usage:
A. He is best player in the team.
B. He is the best player in the team.
C. He is a best player in the team.
D. He is an best player in the team.

options.option_text: A (wrong: 'best' as a superlative must be preceded by 'the': the best, the tallest, the most)
B (correct: THE is used before superlatives — 'the best', 'the tallest', 'the most important' ✓)
C (wrong: 'a best' — indefinite article cannot be used with a superlative)
D (wrong: 'an best' — incorrect on two counts: 'an' before consonant sound AND no article before superlatives)

questions.explanation: B is correct. THE is always used before SUPERLATIVES: the best, the worst, the tallest, the most beautiful, the least expensive. Also used before ordinal numbers (the first, the second, the last). Never use 'a/an' with superlatives.

questions.stem: Choose the correct articles: 'I bought ______ umbrella and ______ book from the market.'

options.option_text: a, a (wrong: 'a umbrella' is incorrect — 'umbrella' begins with vowel sound /ʌ/; needs 'an')
an, a (correct: 'an umbrella' — vowel sound /ʌ/; 'a book' — consonant sound /b/ ✓)
the, the (wrong: 'the' implies specific items already mentioned; 'I bought' suggests first mention)
an, an (wrong: 'an book' — 'book' begins with consonant sound /b/, so 'a book')

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'An umbrella' (umbrella begins with vowel sound /ʌ/) + 'a book' (book begins with consonant sound /b/). Rule: use 'AN' before vowel sounds (a, e, i, o, u sounds) and 'A' before consonant sounds. Both 'an' and 'a' are indefinite articles — used for first mention of non-specific items.

questions.stem: Choose the correct article usage: 'My father is ______ engineer and my mother is ______ doctor.'

options.option_text: a, a (wrong: 'a engineer' — 'engineer' begins with vowel sound /e/; needs 'an')
an, a (correct: 'an engineer' — vowel sound /e/; 'a doctor' — consonant sound /d/ ✓)
the, the (wrong: 'the engineer/doctor' would imply specific, previously-mentioned people)
an, an (wrong: 'an doctor' — 'doctor' begins with consonant sound /d/; use 'a')

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'AN engineer' — 'engineer' begins with vowel sound /ɛ/. 'A doctor' — 'doctor' begins with consonant sound /d/. Indefinite articles before professions: an actor, an artist, an engineer, an officer vs. a teacher, a nurse, a doctor, a lawyer. Also: 'She is A nurse' (profession) — no 'the' unless specific ('She is THE nurse on duty').

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is CORRECT?

options.option_text: We went to a hospital to visit the sick. (wrong: 'a hospital' — for visiting a specific one, should be 'the hospital' OR 'a hospital' if the hospital is not yet specified; actually 'a hospital' works for first mention)
She goes to school by the bus. (wrong: 'by the bus' — for mode of transport, no article is used: 'by bus', 'by car', 'by train')
The milk is good for health. (wrong: 'The milk' implies specific milk; for generic substance: 'Milk is good for health')
She goes to school by bus. (correct: no article with 'by + mode of transport': by bus, by train, by car, by plane ✓)

questions.explanation: D is correct. 'By + vehicle' takes NO article: by bus, by car, by train, by plane, by ship, by bike. Exception: when driving a specific vehicle — 'She came in the car' (her car, specific). Also: go to school (no article = institution, not building), go to the school (= the building), go to bed (no article = function), the bed (specific piece of furniture).

questions.stem: Select the correctly filled sentence: 'He has been waiting for you for ______ hour and ______ half.'

options.option_text: a, a (wrong: 'a hour' is wrong — 'hour' begins with silent H so vowel sound /aʊ/; needs 'an')
an, a (correct: 'an hour' (silent H, vowel sound /aʊ/) and 'a half' (consonant H sound /h/) ✓)
an, an (wrong: 'an half' — 'half' has a pronounced H /h/, so 'a half')
a, an (wrong: 'a hour' is incorrect because H is silent in 'hour')

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'AN hour' — 'hour' has a silent H; pronounced /aʊər/ which begins with vowel sound → 'an'. 'A half' — 'half' has a pronounced H; /hɑːf/ begins with consonant → 'a'. The silent-H rule is critical: hour, honest, honour, heir, heirloom → all take 'an'. Pronounced-H: hotel, house, horse, horse, half, happy → all take 'a'.
